summary: Configured iBGP (AS 65100, extending SONiC's existing instance) between node1 and node2 over a discovered transit link (172.20.0.0/31), so each switch dynamically learns the other's private subnet (192.168.1.0/24 behind node1/node3, 192.168.2.0/24 behind node2/node4) via BGP rather than hand-entered routes. node3 and node4 now reach each other purely via BGP-learned routes. All configuration (interface addressing, forwarding sysctls, BGP peering, and end-host routes) was verified to survive a full reboot of each of the 4 managed nodes, restarted one at a time with confirmed boot-identity changes and post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1/node2 are SONiC-VS switches (BGP AS 65100 preconfigured with ~32 placeholder T0/T2 neighbors); node3/node4 are RHEL7 end hosts each with an unaddressed eth1
Ran SONiC mandatory pre-config cleanup (neutralized docker0, stopped interfaces-config.service) on node1/node2

Empirically discovered the real physical link mapping via targeted ping tests (initial assumption was reversed): node1 eth1 <-> node2 eth1 (transit link), node1 eth2 <-> node3 eth1, node2 eth2 <-> node4 eth1
Assigned 172.20.0.0/31 on the transit link, 192.168.1.0/24 on node1-node3, 192.168.2.0/24 on node2-node4; enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1/node2

Extended the existing SONiC BGP instance (AS 65100) with an iBGP session over the transit link; set a unique BGP router-id on node2 (10.2.0.2, vs node1's 10.1.0.1) to avoid a router-id collision; advertised each private subnet via BGP network statements
Verified the BGP session established and both switches installed each other's private subnet into the kernel FIB via BGP (proto bgp), and confirmed node3<->node4 end-to-end ping success
Persisted interface addressing (/etc/network/interfaces.d/61-antrieb-dre.conf) and forwarding sysctls (/etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf) on node1/node2

Discovered SONiC's bgpcfgd regenerates FRR's BGP config purely from CONFIG_DB at container start, so a manual 'vtysh write memory' alone does not survive reboot; built and enabled a systemd oneshot unit (antrieb-bgp-extend.service) on node1 and node2 that waits for the bgp container/vtysh to be ready and re-applies the neighbor/network config on every boot
Persisted node3/node4 eth1 addressing and static routes via /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-eth1 and route-eth1
Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, BGP state, routes, connectivity) on all 4 nodes, then restarted them one at a time via native 'reboot', polling each until exec access returned
Verified a changed OS boot_id on every node after its restart (node1: 39fdb9ab->abaa65f8, node2: 1eda2df4->06f24811, node3: bdbfa15c->4cedb68b, node4: 0571f4dd->a004ecd8)

After each restart, verified direct proof of recovery: interface addresses/routes restored, BGP session re-established automatically (via the systemd unit on SONiC nodes), BGP routes relearned into the kernel FIB, and end-to-end ping between node3 and node4 succeeding
Performed a final full-mesh verification pass confirming BGP sessions, BGP-learned routes, and node3<->node4 bidirectional reachability are all healthy after all four restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 and node2 learn each other's private network via a routing protocol (not hand-entered routes)
evidence.summary: BGP session established over the transit link (172.20.0.0/31); vtysh 'show ip bgp' and kernel routing table on both node1 and node2 show the peer's private subnet installed with 'proto bgp', not a manually entered static route

evidence.requirement: node3 and node4 can reach each other across the two switches
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping between node3 (192.168.1.2) and node4 (192.168.2.2) succeeds with 0% packet loss, traversing node1 -> transit link -> node2

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before restarts (all 4 nodes)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id, BGP summary, and kernel routes on node1/node2, and boot_id/uptime on node3/node4 prior to any restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed from 39fdb9ab-... to abaa65f8-...; BGP re-established via the persistent systemd unit and node3->node4 ping succeeded post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 1eda2df4-... to 06f24811-...; systemd unit automatically re-applied BGP config (confirmed via systemctl status), BGP session and routes recovered on both node1 and node2, and node4->node1-subnet ping succeeded

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from bdbfa15c-... to 4cedb68b-...; ifcfg-eth1/route-eth1 persisted addressing and route, and post-restart ping to 192.168.2.2 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed from 0571f4dd-... to a004ecd8-...; addressing/route persisted and post-restart ping to 192.168.1.2 succeeded

evidence.requirement: Final full-mesh health check after all 4 restarts
evidence.summary: BGP sessions up on both switches with routes learned via BGP, and node3<->node4 bidirectional ping succeeding with 0% loss
